lede: The one story the web's technologists and its jokers both reached for was Tesla winding down Cybertruck production: 945 points and more than 1,800 comments on Hacker News, plus two separate posts on Lemmy. Wikipedia went somewhere else entirely, handing its day to an article called Ramayana: Part 1 at 785,245 views, about one and a half times the next page down. And the day's largest prediction market was not politics but a basketball game, Trail Blazers against Lakers, where the Lakers sat at better than 99 percent to win.

throughlines.title: Trail Blazers vs. Lakers
throughlines.gist: A single regular-season NBA game was at once a top Google search and the day's biggest prediction market, with the Lakers priced at better than 99 percent to beat Portland.

throughlines.title: Will Abdul El-Sayed win the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination?
throughlines.gist: Abdul El-Sayed surfaced at once on a Wikipedia traffic surge, 437,069 views, and his own 2028 Democratic nomination market, a name drawing attention years ahead of the race.

throughlines.title: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production
throughlines.gist: Tesla's decision to wind down the Cybertruck was the rare story that crossed from Hacker News, at 945 points, to Lemmy, where two posts picked it up: the technical web and the general one agreeing on the same news.
